data.title: A feature item under-declares its globs so the lease refuses the config-section/api-registry/event-template/codegen files its wiring must touch
ddflow MCP server predates the shell code, so MCP tools error on newer knobs and break CLI/MCP parity after a version bump
ddflow MCP server gets a managed restart/upgrade lifecycle: soft upgrade (small detached server, no agent restart), a restart command, a hard kill+respawn, and remote/container reboot

data.claim: A feature item that introduces a new knob/event/command is only given the globs it names, so enforce.commit_without_lease refuses the first write to the shared wiring files (config section + default table, event template, command/parser/api/MCP-tool surfaces); a declarative map keyed by feature class, applied in the single add_task choke point, expands the item's globs before the event is written.
data.falsifier: A task declaring adds=[knob] that lands WITHOUT config_sections/*.py and templates/default.toml in its globs refutes it (the wiring globs are absent).
data.mechanism: services.wiring.WIRING maps knob/event/command to their wiring globs; services.items.add_task appends those globs to the draft's (used to write both the task.added event and the lease) when the draft declares .
data.probe: uv run pytest -q tests/test_task_add_wiring_globs.py tests/test_item_create.py -p no:cacheprovider
data.question: Does task add under-declare the wiring files a new command/knob/event must touch, and can services.items.add_task expand them from a declarative map?

evidence.note: reproduced B-tk-delta-round-empty in a throwaway repo via the failed_review_gate fixture: after a full re-review lands the reviewed head ON the fix (dropping the confirmed finding), ddflow review --delta said 'nothing changed since the reviewed head' and _unchanged_delta answered 'stays failed', so merge refused forever. Related: B10ad449deb (hold shape), B-push-failed-review-delta (converged full guard).

D-failed-review-gate governs: merge/complete refuse a failed review gate unless every confirmed finding is followed by a later delta round that did not raise it. The fix extends the _unchanged_delta release (B10ad449deb) to a confirmed finding whose fix is at the reviewed head, mirroring _held_and_settled, and keeps untriaged findings on 'stays failed'.

Regressed first (test_a_delta_that_is_empty_because_the_fix_is_at_the_reviewed_head_settles_it FAILS on unfixed code: BLOCKER stays after the empty delta), then added the confirmed-finding release to _unchanged_delta. tests/test_complete_failed_review_gate.py + test_review_delta.py + test_review_triage_stale_head.py: 73 passed.

chunk_findings.detail: In `_unchanged_delta`, when `release(counts)` is called for the newly supported case (failed gate with unrechecked confirmed findings, no unreadable findings, and no untriaged findings), `release` uses `counts` which are passed directly from `GD.triage_counts(it, gate) or {}`. However, `counts` returned by `GD.triage_counts` contains triage keys (such as `untriaged`, `refuted`, `confirmed`, etc.), whereas `_settle_mark` expects a counts dictionary containing status categories such as `refuted` and `fixed`, or whichever keys `_settle_mark` counts. Passing `GD.triage_counts` results in an incorrect dictionary structure being passed to `_settle_mark`, causing a `KeyError` or incorrect settling logic when releasing the gate, which can be demonstrated when a failed gate with confirmed findings is released via this branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:649

chunk_findings.detail: `_unchanged_delta` runs for every tree that matches the reviewed head, not only when a later full review already covered a fix. The new branch releases a failed gate as passed whenever `_unrechecked_confirmed` is non-empty, the records are readable, and nothing is untriaged. Given a review that raises finding 1, the user confirms it, and no commit is made, a delta review hits this path and `release()` records the gate passed, so merge proceeds with the confirmed bug still in the tree — the same inputs the old "stays failed" path correctly refused. Nothing in the condition checks that the reviewed head post-dates a fix or that a round actually failed to re-raise the finding.

data.probe: _settle_mark reads counts['refuted'] and counts['confirmed'], both keys GD.triage_counts always returns; 'findings_fixed' is its OUTPUT, not an input the reviewer invented. The release paths in test_review_delta.py + test_complete_failed_review_gate.py pass with no KeyError.

chunk_findings.detail: The new release condition treats any non-empty `dropped` list as enough to mark the whole failed gate passed. `_dropped_unrechecked` only returns confirmed findings absent from the latest `chunk_findings`, and its own comment says a digest the latest record still carries must not be released. Given two unrechecked confirmed findings where the latest record still lists digest B but not digest A, `dropped` is `[(A, ...)]`, `untriaged` is 0, and the `if rec.outcome == "failed" and dropped` branch calls `_release_settled`, recording the gate passed. Merge then accepts an unfixed B that the reviewed head still raised.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:_unchanged_delta

chunk_findings.detail: That same branch passes `GD.triage_counts(...) or {}` into `_release_settled`, which indexes `counts["refuted"]`, `counts["findings"]`, and `counts["confirmed"]` and only guards untriaged with `.get`. The previous use of `triage_counts` only `.get`s `"untriaged"`, so a `None` or partial dict is expected. When `triage_counts` returns `None` (coerced to `{}`) or a dict without those keys, and `dropped` is non-empty, the call either KeyErrors inside the pass text / `_settle_mark`, or treats “counts unavailable” as “no untriaged” and records passed. Input: failed gate, one dropped confirmed digest, `triage_counts` is `None`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:_release_settled

chunk_findings.detail: The release condition is unchanged and still treats any non-empty `dropped` as a whole-gate pass. `_dropped_unrechecked` only omits digests the latest record still lists; it does not require that every unrechecked confirmed finding was omitted. Given two unrechecked confirmed findings where the latest `chunk_findings` still carries digest B but not A, `dropped` is `[(A, ...)]`, `untriaged` is 0, and `if rec.outcome == "failed" and dropped and not counts.get("untriaged")` calls `_release_settled` and records the gate passed. That merges B, which the function’s own comment says must not be released.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:_unchanged_delta

chunk_findings.detail: That same branch still passes `GD.triage_counts(it, gate) or {}` into `_release_settled`, which indexes `counts["refuted"]`, `counts["findings"]`, and `counts["confirmed"]` with no `.get`. The only other use in this function is `counts.get("untriaged", 0)`, so `None` (coerced to `{}`) or a partial dict is an expected return. With `dropped` non-empty and `untriaged` absent, the call KeyErrors on `counts["refuted"]` (the pass text) or inside `_settle_mark`, or treats missing keys as zero and records a pass that was not settled.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:_release_settled
